decision: The Rangers' point-percentage drop (11.8%) mirrors a 14% portfolio loss; misery has company.
anova_analysis: none needed; descriptive comparison
why: Two percent changes set side by side involve no inference to get wrong.

decision: A team of ex-Mets nearly matches the 2026 Mets; the Crow-Armstrong trade is the costliest giveaway.
anova_analysis: t-test of WAR, alumni players vs current Mets players
why: The point rests on summed WAR, which the one-tool analyst would tabulate the same way.

decision: Lindor's .143 is mostly noise; both starting cold is 1-in-77, but Bichette's 53% strikeout rate (1-in-1,430) may be real.
anova_analysis: t-test of per-AB hit and strikeout indicators, 2026 vs career, per player
why: Lindor comes out non-significant (read as 'no change') and Bichette significant, roughly the issue's split, but by t-tests on tiny binary samples rather than event probabilities.

decision: A Mets/Jets/Rangers/ND fan has seen 5 titles in 216 seasons vs Boston's 14; a 32-year drought is a 1-in-185 event.
original_tool: descriptive title counts plus a drought probability
anova_analysis: t-test of per-season title indicator, NY portfolio vs Boston portfolio
why: A t-test on 0/1 title seasons would likely call Boston 'significantly' luckier, same message, but it cannot express the 1-in-185 drought chance.

decision: The Mets' phi = -0.567 with the S&P 500 over 16 days is spurious despite p < .05; do not believe it.
original_tool: phi coefficient with a multiple-comparisons and small-n critique
anova_analysis: t-test of Mets win indicator on market-up vs market-down days
why: The one-tool analyst takes p < .05 as real, which is exactly the error the issue exists to expose.

decision: At 7-14 the Mets' season is bad but not over; the historical base rate leaves real recovery odds.
anova_analysis: t-test of final win% for teams that started 7-14 vs all others
why: A group difference in final win% does not say what this team's odds of recovery are, which is the decision.

decision: At 10-21, recovery odds depend on how the conditional question is framed; an order-of-magnitude difference.
anova_analysis: none possible
why: The tool has no conditional probability of a future outcome, so the lesson cannot be posed.

decision: The Jets' single first-round Hall of Famer in 50 years is the modal league outcome, not an indictment.
anova_analysis: one-way ANOVA of HOF indicator per first-round pick by franchise
why: A non-significant F gives 'Jets are not different', the same verdict, but by reading a null as equality instead of locating the Jets in the distribution.

decision: Williams's 0.33 ERA was partly luck; his true level was always near 3.00, neither 0.33 nor 9.95.
original_tool: regression to the mean / Bayesian update on ERA
anova_analysis: t-test of per-game earned runs, 2026 vs 2020 (or career)
why: A significant drop gets read as a real collapse, where the issue says both extremes were noise around about 3.00.

decision: Stacking ex-All-Star closers fails because reliever ERA barely carries over year to year (r about .25-.35).
anova_analysis: median-split relievers by year-N ERA, t-test year-N+1 ERA
why: With hundreds of relievers the split is significant, so 'good relievers stay good' replaces the issue's point that persistence is weak.

decision: To reach 87 wins the Mets need .578 ball, about their preseason projection; possible, but the remaining games decide it.
anova_analysis: none needed; arithmetic
why: The required pace is division anyone can do; the issue adds no inference beyond comparing it to projections.

decision: Notre Dame is winning both the portal and the 2027 recruiting race, unusual for any program.
anova_analysis: none needed; descriptive
why: Recruiting ranks are reported, not inferred.

decision: Forecast each game as higher-projected team or coin flip within a JND; be honest about uncertainty.
original_tool: prior-based deterministic forecast with JND threshold
anova_analysis: none possible
why: A season forecast of every game is outside the t-test/ANOVA kit.

decision: The 2020 Jets' two late wins cost them Trevor Lawrence: a win worth less than a loss.
anova_analysis: none needed; descriptive
why: The argument is a draft-order fact, with no statistical inference to change.

decision: Sellers did about .039 (six wins) better the next year than holders; the data mostly backs selling, with caution about n = 14.
original_tool: two-group mean comparison with caveats (n=8 vs 6)
anova_analysis: t-test of next-year win%, sellers vs holders
why: With n = 14 the t-test is non-significant, so 'selling makes no difference' replaces the issue's 'small edge, likely real, uncertain'.

decision: Seattle's boom-and-bust swings are what a high-power, low-average lineup produces by design: variance, not a change in the team.
anova_analysis: t-test of runs per game during the win streak vs after
why: The tool compares means rather than spread, so a streak-vs-after difference reads as a team getting hot then cold.

decision: Do not read 'A then B' as 'A caused B'; the Issue #70 error is a media-wide pattern.
anova_analysis: t-test of outcome before vs after an event
why: The one-tool analyst never asks about design, so a before/after comparison commits exactly the error the issue warns about.

decision: The Mets' lopsidedness (mean vs spread of OPS) comes from a weak floor, not the ceiling: Soto alone.
original_tool: 2D scatter of team mean OPS vs within-team SD
anova_analysis: one-way ANOVA of hitter OPS by team
why: ANOVA treats within-team spread as error, which is the very quantity the issue measures.

decision: The 2026 Mets' nearest historical twin is the 2012 Mariners; the next decade depends on strategy.
anova_analysis: none possible
why: Finding analogs by distance and reading their futures is not a group comparison.

decision: A state judge overruling an NCAA ban shows 'banned' no longer carries weight, even though Sorsby withdrew.
anova_analysis: none needed; descriptive
why: No statistical inference is involved.

decision: Wilson won his ring behind a 1,257-yard back; trust the scoreboard over the eye test.
anova_analysis: median-split Wilson seasons by lead-back yards, t-test team wins
why: A split of a dozen seasons would likely point the same way, but with roster quality confounded, the same weakness the issue's anecdote carries.

decision: We call Notre Dame as 2026 national champion, a dated bet beyond what the checklist measures.
original_tool: editorial prediction weighed against a recruiting checklist
anova_analysis: none possible
why: A single-season champion call is a forecast of one event.

decision: Late-season prospect auditions tell you almost nothing; shrunk to the league prior, the Mets' prospects are mostly rough.
anova_analysis: t-test of prospect's per-AB hits vs league average
why: Small n makes the test non-significant, read as 'just average', close to the issue's verdict but without the shrinkage or uncertainty.

decision: With 8 sellers and 22 bidders, whoever wins each rental auction is the one who most overpaid.
original_tool: auction (winner's curse) reasoning on a supply count
anova_analysis: t-test of next-season outcomes, deadline buyers vs non-buyers
why: The winner's-curse prediction is a theoretical forecast, not a group difference.

decision: Coin-flip games like Ohio State-Texas (1.5 points) are the most valuable on the schedule; information has a unit.
anova_analysis: none possible
why: Game value is expressed via win probabilities and bits, which the tool lacks.

decision: A 1-to-138 QB ranking refutes itself: scouts disagree and a QB cannot be ranked apart from his offense.
original_tool: critique of rater agreement and confounded measurement
anova_analysis: none possible
why: The one-tool analyst assumes measurement is error-free, so the ranking's reliability can't be questioned.

decision: Royals 2 titles, Mets 1 despite $830M more; both franchises' totals match what chance owes them.
original_tool: expected titles under chance vs observed
anova_analysis: t-test of per-season title indicator, Mets vs Royals
why: A non-significant test gives 'money made no difference', close to the issue's verdict, but it cannot compute the chance-expected title count.

decision: A point spread is a probability in disguise (-7 is about 70%) and is well calibrated.
anova_analysis: one-sample t-test of (margin minus spread) vs 0
why: The test can show the spread is unbiased but cannot turn it into a win probability, which is the reader's takeaway.

decision: Only 21 of 133 top departments earn more than they spend; Ohio State is the exception, not the rule.
original_tool: descriptive count of the full distribution
anova_analysis: one-sample t-test of revenue minus expense vs 0
why: A significant negative mean gives the same 'most lose money' decision.

decision: Velocity and K rate stabilize fast, ERA takes a season and a half; trust the early-settling numbers.
anova_analysis: median-split early ERA, t-test of later ERA
why: Reliability as a function of sample size can't be posed by a tool that assumes stats are measured without error.

decision: Invite all 365, seed off ten games, double elimination: 59% fewer games and the best team wins 55% vs 45%.
anova_analysis: none possible
why: Comparing bracket formats needs simulation of title probabilities.

decision: Teams 1-2 ranks apart split 48.7/51.3; a ranking needs about 10 places to mean anything.
original_tool: win rates by rank gap, two independent methods
anova_analysis: one-way ANOVA of higher-ranked win indicator by rank-gap bin; t-tests vs .5
why: Small gaps come out non-significant and read as 'no difference', near the issue's answer, but the threshold would move with sample size, not effect size.

decision: 'Hot' depends on window length; the 7-straight Royals are a .435 team.
anova_analysis: t-test of win indicator, last 7-10 games vs rest of season
why: A short-window t-test can call the Royals significantly hot; the tool never questions the chosen window.

decision: How a club reached the playoffs does not reliably predict October success (p = .055, intervals overlap); score the experience separately.
original_tool: simulated weekly odds, grouped series win rates with 95% intervals
anova_analysis: one-way ANOVA (or t-test) of series win indicator across midseason-odds groups
why: p = .055 gives 'no difference', near the issue's shrug, but as proof of absence rather than an overlapping-interval gap that 'if anything' points the other way.

decision: The SEC's schedule edge is real but only 0.4 points; conference is a small part of schedule strength.
anova_analysis: t-test of schedule strength, SEC vs Big Ten teams
why: A non-significant SEC-B1G test says 'no edge', practically near the issue, but loses the size and the poll-free rating behind it.

decision: Home field is a constant +0.14 in log-odds: worth 3.5 points to a coin-flip club, 1.2 to a dominant one.
anova_analysis: t-test of win indicator, home vs away
why: The t-test returns one percentage-point home edge for everyone, the additive-probability error the issue debunks.

decision: Our ratings do not beat the line (51.0% over 2,140 games, interval includes 50); a perfect 15/15 backtest was leakage.
anova_analysis: one-sample t-test of cover indicator vs .5
why: On the leaky 15/15 data the test is wildly significant and the tool never asks about design, so 'we have an edge' would stand.

decision: Time of possession predicts second-half scoring only because teams with the ball are ahead (+0.216 to -0.003).
anova_analysis: median-split time of possession, t-test second-half points
why: The one-way split is significant and read as possession helping; the tool does not ask about the score confound.

decision: Mississippi State's 25-point win moved Minnesota's rating 8x more than the winner's; the game was about the loser.
anova_analysis: none possible
why: There is no rating model to update, so who the game informed about can't be asked.

decision: Over 40 seasons, $84K through a pool ends near $80K; the same money in an index fund ends near $167K.
original_tool: historical compounding over every start year
anova_analysis: paired or two-sample t-test of ending balance, bettor vs index across start years
why: The gap is so large that any comparison gives the same decision, even with overlapping windows.

decision: A first-year coach wins about one game fewer than his inherited talent should; he climbs as the roster becomes his.
original_tool: talent-adjusted residuals by coach year with within-career survivor check
anova_analysis: one-way ANOVA of raw win% by coach tenure year
why: Raw win% rises with tenure too, but it confounds inherited talent and survivors, the two things the issue controls.

decision: Six unranked-over-ranked upsets is low, but from the most chances since 2019; favorites held more than usual.
anova_analysis: t-test of per-game upset indicator, 2026 vs 2019-25
why: A per-game comparison uses the denominator, which is the issue's whole point.

decision: Bills and Notre Dame are our picks yet only about 15% and 16% each; both together about 1 in 40.
anova_analysis: none possible
why: Championship probabilities need simulation.

decision: The Rays beat a regression forecast by 19 wins; champions usually beat theirs (22 of 25).
anova_analysis: t-test of win change (this year minus last) for champions vs non-champions
why: Raw win change still shows champions improving, but ignores that strong teams regress, understating the surprise.

decision: RBI measure opportunity as much as hitting: hitting quality explains 43%, add runners on and power and about 90%.
anova_analysis: median-split hitters by OPS, t-test RBI
why: A significant split 'confirms' RBI measure hitting; the tool treats the stat as meaning the same for every lineup slot.

decision: 54 of 74 programs with 1,000+ games sit outside the coin-flip funnel; records do not even out.
anova_analysis: one-sample t-test of each program's win indicator vs .5
why: With 1,000+ games, a t-test vs .5 is effectively the issue's funnel.

decision: A 60-year-old Jets fan likely outlives Woody Johnson but has worse than even odds of seeing the team leave the family.
original_tool: base rates from 28 owner deaths, actuarial reasoning
anova_analysis: none possible
why: Survival and succession odds are time-to-event probabilities.

decision: Chicago traded about seven later starter-seasons for 2-3 sooner, better ones from Simmons.
original_tool: comparable-player base rates of future starter seasons
anova_analysis: t-test of seasons started, late-first-round picks vs DT comps
why: Forecasting future seasons for one player and two picks is outside the kit.

decision: A questionable player plays about 2 times in 3 (9,634 of 14,346); start there, then adjust.
original_tool: base rate from NFL injury reports
anova_analysis: none possible
why: The issue's decision is one player's chance of playing, and the tool has no single-event probability.

decision: In college, answer drives score 32 per 100 vs 35 on other drives; most of the gap is the scoreboard, not heart.
original_tool: drive-level rates with game-state adjustment, by season
anova_analysis: t-test of drive-scored indicator, answer drives vs other kickoff drives
why: With about 9,000 games the gap is significant and reads as teams wilting after a TD; the tool does not separate the scoreboard.

decision: College NIL spending is highly unequal (Gini 0.37); the EO would compress it toward Notre Dame's level.
anova_analysis: t-test of NIL spending, P4 vs G5
why: A large significant group gap tells the same 'very unequal' story, without the Gini.

decision: JUCO-to-D1 arrivals sidestep the one-transfer cap; that is the future of college baseball under the EO.
anova_analysis: none needed; descriptive
why: A rules argument with an example; no inference to change.
